title: Cyclone Akvan: Over 80,000 Evacuated in Odisha as Landfall Nears Friday Noon
excerpt: Evacuations have risen past 80,000 against a 2-lakh target, 74 rescue teams are deployed, and the IMD now fixes Akvan's landfall between Narsapur and Puri, close to east of Gopalpur, by noon on Friday, November 20.
body:
• Odisha has now evacuated more than 80,000 people — up from about 50,000 reported on Wednesday — against a target of 2 lakh, as severe cyclonic storm Akvan approaches, officials said on Thursday, November 19.
  • The IMD's morning bulletin fixes landfall between Narsapur in Andhra Pradesh and Puri in Odisha, close to east of Gopalpur, by noon on Friday, November 20, with maximum sustained winds of 90–100 kmph gusting to 110 kmph.
  • Seventy-four rescue teams are deployed across 11 districts; 308 shelters are operational with free kitchens, 36,398 people had been shifted in Ganjam alone by 6 a.m. Thursday, and 1,098 pregnant women have been moved to safety.
  • Travel is disrupted: trains have been cancelled and rescheduled, including services on the Visakhapatnam–Kirandul route on November 19 and 20, and the weekly Chennai–Yangon flight has been cancelled in both directions.

Odisha has evacuated more than 80,000 people and deployed 74 rescue teams as severe cyclonic storm Akvan closes in on the Andhra Pradesh–Odisha coast, officials said on Thursday, November 19. The evacuation, which Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi put at around 50,000 people on Wednesday, has since been sped up against a state target of 2 lakh people, a Revenue and Disaster Management Department official said, according to PTI reporting in The Hindu BusinessLine. This updates our earlier coverage of the storm's track; the landfall point and timing are now fixed more precisely.

Where the storm is, and when it crosses

The India Meteorological Department (IMD), in its morning bulletin, said the severe cyclonic storm over the west-central Bay of Bengal moved northwards at 12 kmph during the six hours to 5:30 a.m. and lay centred about 440 km east-southeast of Narsapur in Andhra Pradesh, 530 km south of Gopalpur in Odisha and 590 km south of Puri. The system is likely to cross the north Andhra Pradesh and south Odisha coasts between Narsapur and Puri, close to east of Gopalpur, by Friday noon, retaining severe cyclonic storm intensity with maximum sustained winds of 90–100 kmph gusting to 110 kmph.

The Met office issued a red warning for Kendrapara, Jagatsinghpur, Puri, Ganjam, Gajapati and Kandhamal districts for Thursday, forecasting heavy to very heavy rainfall, and warned of very heavy to extremely heavy rainfall across 11 districts on Thursday and Friday. A storm surge of 0.5 to 1 metre above the astronomical tide is likely to inundate low-lying areas of Ganjam and Puri districts. Squally winds of 40–50 kmph, gusting to 60 kmph, are already prevailing along the south Odisha coast, and coastal and southern parts of the state have had light to moderate rain since Wednesday night, with intensity expected to increase gradually.

Evacuation and rescue, district by district

Ganjam, expected to be the worst hit, had shifted 36,398 people to shelters by 6 a.m. on Thursday, with evacuation still under way, an official said. Altogether 308 shelters are operational, with free kitchens serving the evacuated people, and 1,098 pregnant women have been shifted safely. In Ganjam, four Odisha Disaster Rapid Action Force (ODRAF) teams, three National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) teams, 24 Fire and Emergency Services teams and 10 Odisha Forest Development Corporation teams have been deployed across all blocks.

The 74 rescue teams are deployed across Malkangiri, Koraput, Rayagada, Kalahandi, Gajapati, Ganjam, Kandhamal, Boudh, Puri, Nayagarh and Khurda districts. The state government has closed educational institutes in districts under red, orange and yellow warnings. The region is recovering from two recent cyclones, which is why officials have set a zero-casualty aim for this landfall, as we reported in our earlier coverage of Akvan's track.

Trains and flights disrupted

Railway authorities have cancelled two trains between Visakhapatnam and Koraput on Thursday and Friday, The Hindu BusinessLine reported. Jagran Josh, citing railway updates reported by IANS, listed three express trains rescheduled on November 19: the Charlapalli–Shalimar East Coast Express (18046), moved from 8:40 a.m. to 3:40 p.m.; the Secunderabad–Howrah Falaknuma Express (12704), from 3:55 p.m. to 5:55 p.m.; and the SMVT Bengaluru–Muzaffarpur Express (15227), from 12:30 a.m. to 8:30 a.m. The Visakhapatnam–Kirandul Express (18515) and the Kirandul–Visakhapatnam Express (18516) will not operate on November 19 and 20.

The weekly Chennai–Yangon flight has been cancelled in both directions because of the cyclone, Jagran Josh reported, with more than 144 passengers who had travelled to Chennai to board it affected.

What happens next

The storm is expected to make landfall close to east of Gopalpur around noon on Friday, November 20. Evacuation continues through Thursday in the districts in the storm's path, and rainfall intensity is forecast to rise as Akvan approaches. Readers with family in coastal Odisha or north Andhra Pradesh should expect further train and flight changes on Friday and check with the railways or their airline before travelling.
